transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-26
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya R (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (MidBridge CTO), Markus (Platform), Priya N (ML), Evan (SRE)
---
Summary: Quick discovery to map integration paths. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) and how Redwood integrates with their gateway/proxy and LangChain/LlamaIndex stacks. Want code examples, observability hooks, rate-limit behaviour and starting POC plan.
Topics: SDKs (py/node), LangChain adapter, LlamaIndex connector, gateway-sidecar vs proxy, rate limits/quotas, observability/tracing, security (SOC2, KMS, SSO), pilot scope
---
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros then we can jump into your stack — Lena?
[00:12] Lena (CTO): Hi, Lena here, we run MidBridge analytics, focus on customer analytics pipelines for retail. We're evaluating inference platforms for our recommendation and search embedding pipelines.
[00:20] Markus (Platform): Markus, infra. We're particularly worried about latency spikes on peak loads and also data isolation.
[00:28] Jordan (AE): Great. Priya R (SE) and Samir are with me from Redwood. We'll try to map the integration options — SDK and gateway patterns then go into security and POC asks.
[00:37] Priya R (SE): Awesome. Quick question — what does your app call path look like today? LangChain, LlamaIndex in the middle or do you have a custom gateway?
[00:45] Priya N (ML Eng): We use LangChain orchestration in python for a lot of retrieval-augmented generation, and LlamaIndex for our doc store connectors. We also have an internal API gateway — it's a lightweight proxy that routes to model endpoints and applies quotas.
[00:58] Evan (SRE): The gateway is an envoy-based proxy with sidecars for some microservices. We do token buckets at the gateway and maintain per-tenant quotas.
[01:07] Samir (SE): Cool — that gives us options. We usually see customers integrate via: 1) direct SDK in app (py/node), 2) LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter using our SDK or HTTP, or 3) route through an internal gateway/proxy that forwards to Redwood. Each has tradeoffs for latency vs centralized control.
[01:26] Lena (CTO): Our preference is to keep gateway control for quotas, but we want minimal extra latency. How much overhead does a gateway add compared to direct hosted calls?
[01:36] Priya R (SE): There's some overhead from an extra hop — tends to be tens of milliseconds on our hosted infra, but p95 depends on payload sizes and batching. With prefix/K V cache enabled and proper batching, you can often keep p95 in the low hundreds for medium sequences. Sorry, K V — the transcriber: KV cache.
[01:52] Markus (Platform): When you say KV cache, do you mean prefix caching at the runtime? How is that exposed to customers?
[01:58] Priya R (SE): Right, it's prefix/KV cache, we expose config in the model route: cache TTL, cache keys, and automatic prefix reuse for repeated prompts. For gateway setups we recommend passing a session id or conversation id in headers so the runtime can reuse KV efficiently.
[02:12] Lena (CTO): Okay. On security: SOC2 and SSO are must-haves. For private deployments we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs.
[02:20] Jordan (AE): We can share the SOC2 pack and our private deployment security sheet. For VPC deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; audit logs are retained per your retention policy. We'll send details.
[02:32] Evan (SRE): For our compliance team, are there options to run the Redwood control plane in our VPC or is it fully managed?
[02:39] Samir (SE): Private deployment options include a customer-controlled control plane (VPC) and an on-prem bundle for air-gapped. There are some tradeoffs in upgrades and observability access. We provide telemetry hooks that push to your telemetry backend or we can configure forwarders.
[02:55] Priya N (ML Eng): Observability is key — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency histograms for our model routes. Does Redwood expose tracing spans?
[03:04] Priya R (SE): Yes, we have tracing hooks; you can forward OpenTelemetry spans. We also have per-request metadata in logs: model, route, tokens in/out, quantization variant, and batch id. For LangChain integrations we have middleware that attaches trace ids to calls so traces stitch across your app and our runtime.
[03:22] Markus (Platform): That middleware — is it a langchain callback or a full SDK wrapper?
[03:27] Samir (SE): We ship both: lightweight SDK wrappers (py/node) and LangChain callback adapters. For LlamaIndex we provide a connector that uses the same underlying client, and there are examples for async streaming.
[03:39] Lena (CTO): Streaming: we need server-sent events for chat UX, and backpressure handling. Do you support streaming with gateway proxies?
[03:47] Priya R (SE): Streaming works over websocket/SSE for hosted APIs. If you pass through a gateway, ensure it supports websocket passthrough or we recommend a sidecar pattern where the service calls Redwood directly and the gateway handles auth and quotas. Proxies sometimes buffer which breaks streaming.
[04:02] Evan (SRE): That's our fear — envoy default config does buffer. So sidecar seems safer. But that increases number of egress clients. Any recommendations on egress cost vs central proxy?
[04:12] Jordan (AE): Common pattern: gateway for control plane (quotas, routing decisions) but sidecar for streaming-heavy endpoints. Or use a thin gateway layer that routes to your service which then does direct calls. We'll add pattern docs.
[04:24] Priya N (ML Eng): On cost control — we have many small LLM calls for embeddings and many long context chains for RAG. How does Redwood's batching/quantization recommendation workflow work?
[04:34] Priya R (SE): Redwood Optimize gives quantization and batching suggestions based on your token distribution. We can run a profiling pass against a sample workload and recommend model variants (int8, int4), batch sizes and cache settings. For embeddings we often recommend batched embedding calls. We'll need a sample dataset or traffic profile for that.
[04:50] Markus (Platform): That profiling will need sample QPS and p95 targets. We're targeting 99th percentile latency < 350ms for inference on our search endpoint under 200 QPS. Is that feasible on hosted?
[05:01] Samir (SE): Possibly for smaller models and with autoscaling. For bigger 2.xB models or long sequence lengths you'd probably want Dedicated capacity to guarantee p95. We can run bench tests during the POC.
[05:12] Lena (CTO): Timeline: we want a pilot in 6 weeks. Must include SRE, ML, and product sign-off.
[05:18] Jordan (AE): Sounds good — typical pilot is a 4-week POC: week 0 scoping + instrument, week 1 profile + baseline, week 2 integration + tests, week 3 validation and docs. We'll align on success metrics.
[05:29] Priya R (SE): For the POC we should decide an integration pattern. Given your envoy buffering concern and desire to keep quota control, I'd recommend: gateway handles auth/quotas, services run sidecar client that calls Redwood directly for streaming and high-throughput; for embeddings we can have a batched async worker that uses the SDK. That minimizes buffering impact and keeps quotas centralized.
[05:51] Markus (Platform): That sounds ok. What about SSO and RBAC for who can deploy models and see logs?
[05:58] Samir (SE): We support SSO/SAML and role-based access. On Dedicated/Private you can map to your identity provider. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM.
[06:07] Priya N (ML Eng): LangChain — are there any gotchas with our current langchain version? We're on 0.2x something.
[06:13] Priya R (SE): We have examples for 0.2x and 0.3x; the main gotchas are streaming callback chain and async vs sync client differences. We'll provide snippets for your exact version. Also LlamaIndex connector will require a small adapter for chunking config.
[06:28] Lena (CTO): Pricing — can you give us a rough hosted vs dedicated TCO? We want an estimate by next week to build a business case.
[06:36] Jordan (AE): We'll send a ballpark TCO worksheet. Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is commit-based and better if you have steady high QPS or strict isolation requirements. For private on-prem there's a platform fee plus support. We'll include expected token/unit cost comparisons and examples.
[06:51] Evan (SRE): Legal/procurement: we need SOC2 docs and DPAs. We also require a security questionnaire; do you have a standard packet?
[06:58] Jordan (AE): Yes, I'll attach the standard security pack and DPA. For procurement we'll include contract templates for dedicated and private.
[07:07] Priya R (SE): One more technical note — rate limiting and quotas: Redwood enforces per-api-key quotas server-side, but if you want strict per-tenant rate limits we recommend enforcing at the gateway as primary with server-side fallbacks in Redwood. We also support per-route rate caps and burst windows in the route config.
[07:25] Markus (Platform): If gateway is primary rate limiter, do we lose some observability fidelity?
[07:30] Samir (SE): You can still forward request ids and traces; both sides record token usage. We'll correlate via trace id. So you get end-to-end visibility in your telemetry.
[07:39] Lena (CTO): Ok last thing — what's needed from us to prepare the POC?
[07:43] Priya R (SE): Sample traffic profile, infra diagram, a small corpus for embedding profiling, list of endpoints and success metrics. Also ssh or access plan for integrating private VPC if you choose that route.
[07:54] Jordan (AE): We'll follow up with a scoping doc and sample code.
[07:58] Lena (CTO): Great, thank you.
---
Recap (by Jordan):
- Integration pattern recommendation: gateway for quotas + sidecar direct calls for streaming and high-throughput embeddings.
- Provide SDK examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex, and raw HTTP.
- Share SOC2/security pack, private deployment docs, and TCO worksheet.
- POC target: start in ~6 weeks, 4-week pilot.
